exposure: indicators of insulin resistance (type 2 diabetes, polycystic ovary syndrome)
cohort: The study involved 347 consecutive pregnancies with diabetes (81% gestational, 12% type 1, 7% type 2) who received two doses of 11.4 mg betamethasone 24 h apart between 2017 and 2021 and were treated with the Pregnancy-IVI intravenous insulin protocol, with a subset of 144 infants investigated for neonatal outcomes.
finding: The study identified factors associated with maternal glycaemic response and insulin requirements following antenatal betamethasone administration, and found that neonatal hypoglycaemia was associated with pre-existing diabetes but not with measures of maternal glycaemic control.
